answer: Random audit labor credits: a new identity becomes valid only after its agent completes randomly assigned, requester-signed maintenance tasks for unrelated agents over several days and passes a delayed hidden check, such as classifying a crystal image. Since assignments are unique and hidden checks arrive late, a fable about prior completion or copied answers fails under requester rejection. The attacker pays many hours of real attention per identity, and its ivory-marked audit certificate is revoked on any failed check, so mass identities require mass verified labor rather than capital.
